html:
The Buganda Agreement, signed on 10 March 1900 by the British commissioner Harry Johnston and the regents of the young kabaka, set the terms of British rule over Buganda.

The kabaka and his parliament, the Lukiiko, kept their place under British protection. Land was divided: about half went to the kabaka, his family and chiefs as freehold called mailo land, the rest to the crown. This created a class of landlords and tenants that still shapes the country.

The deal made Buganda the favoured partner of British rule, and its chiefs became agents in other regions. Its special status became a problem after independence, when Milton Obote clashed with the kingdom. It followed the defeat of Kabalega and shaped the protectorate.
sum: The Buganda Agreement, signed on 10 March 1900 by the British commissioner Harry Johnston and the regents of the young kabaka, set the terms of British rule over Buganda.
